title: Investigate negative SST variance after the second-moment fix
status: PROVISIONAL — do not submit as a confirmed erratum
description: The older tossq bug was fixed, but subtracting mean SST squared from the published SST second moment can still give a negative variance. That may come from precision or cancellation in the native moments rather than a remaining formula mistake.
example: January 0101 piControl reaches −0.0119001 °C². A standard-deviation calculation takes the square root and returns an invalid result, because a mathematical variance cannot be negative.
scientific_evidence: The old tossq=mean(tos)² defect is not reproduced in the current monthly sample. But tossq−tos² reaches −0.0119001 °C² in January 0101 piControl, which is inconsistent with a mathematical variance. Cancellation in the converted native moments or float32 precision is a plausible explanation, not yet a demonstrated root cause. Fourteen tossq datasets share the product family; this is not a claim that all fourteen have been shown to violate the inequality.

recommended_action: Compare native first and second moments at matched time support, inspect packing and precision, and quantify negative-variance cells before issuing an erratum or changing moments.
development_team_action: MOPPy and MOM/ocean developers: compare matched native first/second moments, units, packing and precision. Identify where precision is lost before choosing a correction. Do not blindly clamp second moments or change an entire archive based on one diagnostic.
extent_statement: Investigation scope only; files are not established to be defective.
publication_action: No withdrawal, retraction, replacement or ESGF submission performed by this task.
